pages.text: What a generator burns is a recipe, so a datapack can add to it or replace it. You do not need a mod, and you do not need KubeJS.$(br2)Put a file in your datapack at $(o)data/<your pack>/recipe/anything.json$() and it works the moment the pack loads. It shows up in JEI too.

pages.title: The file
pages.text: $(#555){$(br)  "type": "ultimatetransport:generator_fuel",$(br)  "generator": "fuel_generator",$(br)  "fuel": { "item": "minecraft:coal" },$(br)  "burn_time": 1600$(br)}$()$(br2)$(l)generator$(): fuel_generator, lava_generator or nether_star_generator.$(br)$(l)fuel$(): any ingredient, so $(#555){ "tag": "c:coals" }$() works.$(br)$(l)burn_time$(): ticks it burns for.

pages.title: Changing the output
pages.text: Add $(l)rate$() to make that one fuel produce a different amount:$(br2)$(#555)"rate": 500$()$(br2)Leave it out and the generator's own rate is used, which is what you usually want. The rate itself is in the config, under $(o)generators$().

pages.title: With KubeJS
pages.text: This mod ships a KubeJS plugin, so the type has a proper builder. No $(o)event.custom$() needed:$(br2)$(#555)ServerEvents.recipes(event => {$(br)  event.recipes.ultimatetransport$(br)    .generator_fuel($(br)      'lava_generator',$(br)      'minecraft:magma_block',$(br)      700)$(br)})$()$(br2)The fourth argument is the optional rate.
